entries.topicDescription: Creating domain-specific languages using Kotlin's builder pattern.

tips.title: Building a type-safe HTML DSL
tips.content:
Kotlin DSLs combine lambdas with receivers, extension functions,
and operator overloading to create readable, type-safe mini-languages.

The compiler ensures you can only nest valid elements.
You can't put a <td> directly inside a <html> — the types prevent it.

Popular Kotlin DSLs: Ktor routing, Gradle Kotlin DSL, Compose UI,
kotlinx.html, and Exposed (SQL).

tips.title: @DslMarker — scoping DSL receivers
tips.content:
Without @DslMarker, nested lambdas can access outer receivers implicitly.
This leads to confusing bugs where you call a method on the wrong scope.

@DslMarker creates an annotation that restricts implicit receiver access.
Members of the outer receiver are hidden inside inner lambdas —
you must use explicit 'this@outer' to access them.

Always use @DslMarker in production DSLs to prevent scope leaking.

tips.title: Lambda with receiver — the DSL foundation
tips.content:
A lambda with receiver lets you call methods on an object inside a lambda
as if you were inside that class. The receiver becomes 'this'.

This is the core mechanism behind Kotlin DSLs and builder patterns.
Functions like apply, with, and buildString all use this concept.

Signature: ClassName.() -> Unit means "a lambda where 'this' is ClassName."
